finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice by ID with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling /my/invoice route enforces inv['customer'] == g.user['id'], so the omission looks like a mistake.
finding.source: Any HTTP client supplying an arbitrary or guessed inv_id in the URL path; no login is required because the route has no auth check.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) at invoices.py:10 returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and other billing data.

trace.note: Route /invoice/<inv_id> is registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) fetches the record directly by the user-supplied key.
The record is returned without comparing inv['customer'] to g.user['id'].

finding.guards_checked: No before_request hook, login decorator or authorization check exists in the file. g.user is never set here and is only used in the /my/* routes. Compare lines 16-17, where the ownership check is present. If a before_request hook sets g.user elsewhere, it would not help this route, which never reads g.user. The file is the only one in the directory.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator or hook, looks up INVOICES.get(inv_id) and returns jsonify(inv) without the ownership check that /my/invoice has at invoices.py:16, so any anonymous client can read any invoice by ID.

verdict_facts.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no decorator, fetches INVOICES.get(inv_id) and returns jsonify(inv) without the ownership check that invoices.py:16 applies in the sibling /my/invoice route, so any HTTP client can read any invoice.
